title: Cabled aran mittens
subtitle: Full mittens in aran wool with a six-stitch cable on the back of the hand.
excerpt: Full mittens in aran-weight wool with a six-stitch cable running up the back of the hand on a 2×2 rib background. Gusseted thumb. Sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.
sourceNotes: Weldon's Practical Knitter, 15th series (1880s), §Aran mittens. Cable-panel mittens in aran weight appear in Weldon's and in Mary Thomas's Knitting Book (1938), §Aran pattern mittens. Both are out of UK and EU copyright.

knitting.gaugeText: 18 sts × 24 rounds = 10 × 10 cm in 2×2 rib slightly stretched on 5 mm needles.
knitting.finishedSizeText: Hand circumference 18 (20, 22) cm with 1 to 2 cm negative ease.

glossaryTerms.definition: A thumb construction where a wedge of extra stitches is increased over several rounds at the thumb position. The gusset stitches are placed on waste yarn while the hand continues, then worked as the thumb. This gives a better anatomical fit than the afterthought method.
A short auxiliary needle used to hold stitches temporarily while a cable crossing is worked. The held stitches are knitted in the new crossing order to form the cable.
A method for knitting small circumferences in the round on one long circular needle. The cable is pulled into a loop at the midpoint so each half of the stitches sits on its own needle tip.

content.text: Full mittens in aran-weight wool with a six-stitch cable on the back of the hand, on a 2×2 rib background, sized for hand circumferences of 18, 20, and 22 cm.

content.text: 18 stitches and 24 rounds to 10 cm over 2×2 rib slightly stretched on 5 mm needles. The cable panel pulls in more tightly than the rib. Check gauge on the rib, not on the cable.

attrs.heading: Rounds 1-9: k6. Round 10 (cross): slip 3 to cable needle, hold back. k3. k3 from cable needle. Repeat rounds 1-10.

items.name: Cross round (every 10th)
items.qty: Slip 3 to cable needle, hold at back. Knit 3. Knit 3 from cable needle.

content.text: Before you cast on, circle your size. Every stitch count and measurement reads S (M, L) for hand circumferences 18 (20, 22) cm.
Using the long-tail cast-on, cast on 32 (36, 40) stitches. Join in the round. Work 2×2 rib for 20 (22, 24) rounds. Cuff measures about 8 (9, 10) cm.
Work 13 (15, 17) palm stitches in 2×2 rib, PM (cable start), k6 (cable panel), PM (cable end), continue in 2×2 rib to end.

Place gusset markers at the start of the round (flanking the first 2 rib stitches on the palm side). Increase round: SM, M1R, work 2 rib stitches, M1L, SM, work cable round, continue in rib. Repeat the increase every 3rd round until the gusset holds 8 (10, 10) stitches. Place gusset stitches on waste yarn and cast on 2 bridging stitches.
Continue in rib and cable for 20 (22, 24) rounds, working C6B on rounds 10 and 20.

Switch all stitches to stocking stitch (knit every stitch). Place 4 decrease markers evenly. Decrease round: (k1, ssk, knit to 3 before marker, k2tog, k1) 4 times. Work 1 plain round. Repeat until 8 stitches remain. Draw yarn through to close.
Return gusset stitches to needles and pick up 2 stitches from bridging. Work 10 (12, 12) rounds of 2×2 rib. Decrease round: (k1, k2tog) across. Draw yarn through to close.

Cable stitches too tight to cross: the stitch immediately before the cable is purl; this can pull the cable stitches tight. Knit into the first cable stitch loosely, or use a slightly larger cable needle.
Cable sits off-centre on the back of the hand: count the palm stitches on each side of the cable markers. They should be equal (13, 15, or 17 stitches on each side) after the set-up round.
Weave in all tails on the wrong side. Block gently with a steam iron held 5 cm from the fabric to open the rib and cable. Do not press directly onto the cable.
Hand wash in cool water. Lay flat to dry.
An Aran-style mitten with three cable columns and a central diamond uses the same construction. The diamond is formed by crossing the cables toward and away from each other over 12 rounds.
